title: How to organize the board game and puzzle zone | Family Room
description:
Store games and puzzles so that anything you pull off the shelf is complete and playable tonight.

This is the Board Game and Puzzle Zone in the Family Room. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Boxes lying flat in stacks no more than five high, each with a strip of tape on the short edge naming the game so you can read it from the doorway, every loose piece bagged inside its own lid, and not one box on the shelf that failed its count.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Open every box and count the pieces against the list printed on the rules sheet.
Straighten: Games lie flat and stack by height, heaviest at the bottom, tallest boxes on the lower shelf.
Shine: Wipe the box lids and edges, which pick up a surprising film in a room where people eat.

Standardize: Tape on the short edge with the name, plus a date written on the lid the last time the box passed a count.
Sustain: On game night, the count happens as the box goes back, not as it comes out, so the next person is never the on

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Every box on the shelf has passed a piece count with the date on its lid, loose pieces are bagged inside their own box, and the name is readable on the short edge from across the room.
